note: Mobile app performance monitoring (San Francisco), Crittercism until its 2015 rename to Apteligent; the base carried both names and they are one row since the rebuild. Google Ventures was in the $1.2M seed announced 2011-07-13 with Kleiner Perkins, Opus, Shasta and AOL Ventures (TechCrunch), re-upped in the $5.5M Series A of June 2012 (TechCrunch, 2012-06-01) and led the $12M Series B of March 2013 (TechCrunch, 2013-03-12), so the entry is the seed, not the B the Apteligent row had read; the named Series A graduates it. A $30M round with Accenture followed in April 2014. Acquired by VMware in 2017 (the firm's own exit line; VMware announced it on 2017-05-15).

funding_rounds.lead: Opus Capital; Shasta Ventures; Google Ventures

note: Acute and transitional care at home, founded in New Orleans in 2016 as Ready Responders (readyresponders.com, the firm's 2020-23 listing, same partner) and operating as myLaurel since 2023; the base carried both names and they are one row since the rebuild. GV was among the investors in Ready's $54M Series C (Home Health Care News, 2020-09-16), which says GV, Deerfield and City Light put over $100M in across two rounds in under a year, so GV may have entered in the preceding round, also Growth; the entry date is the Series C's. The $12M initial closing of June 2025 was 'led by Deerfield Management and GV' (the company's release) and SteelSky Ventures led a further round in November 2025 with GV a previous investor. Headquarters New York (the company's release).

Live-services backend and SDK for game developers, relaunched in 2020 from the 'Boston-based' game studio Disruptor Beam (TechCrunch 2017-02-02, 2020-04-21), which went through a Subchapter V reorganization. Rounds read: $3.2M Series A (GrandBanks), a 2017 Series B led by GrandBanks and Romulus, and a $5M round in February 2021 led by Companyon Ventures and GrandBanks (GamesBeat); none names GV, so undetermined; the firm listed the company as Disruptor Beam from 2013 (under Rich Miner) and as Beamable from 2020, one row since the rebuild. Skillz acquired Beamable in January 2026 (Wikipedia).

Epigenetic editing, formed in December 2024 when Chroma Medicine and Nvelop Therapeutics merged into nChroma Bio with a $75M financing from 19 firms led by Cormorant, Arch, Atlas and Newpath; BioPharma Dive names GV among the investors the two companies already had in common. The company's own site gives 201 Brookline Avenue, Boston. Entry read through the predecessor: GV led Chroma Medicine's $135M Series B (the company's release of 2023-03-01, Cambridge MA dateline), and its list of existing investors does not include GV, so the Series B was the firm's first money in the business; Chroma had launched in November 2021 with $125M seeded by Atlas and Newpath. The two predecessors are one row with this company since the rebuild. The firm's live list files nChroma Bio under Issi Rozen, Chroma's GV partner, which is why the entry is read through Chroma; GV's other predecessor position, Nvelop's $100M seed of about 2022 (GEN, 2024-04), is recorded here, not as a second entry. No priced valuation disclosed.
